title: Share Location Link Generator: Every Map App
description: Turn coordinates into Google Maps, OpenStreetMap and Bing links with the Share Location Link Generator — one pair, every provider. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, Times Square's pair 40.7580, −73.9855 becomes three different links — one per provider — that all open on exactly the same crossroads in Manhattan.
quick_answer: The Share Location Link Generator turns one latitude/longitude pair into ready-to-send links for Google Maps, OpenStreetMap and Bing Maps. Enter the coordinates once, pick a zoom, and copy the provider link your recipient prefers — the same WGS84 point, dressed in each service's own URL format.

A link opens centred on the exact spot, zoom set close. In a stressful moment nobody should be reading digits aloud.

Google's format carries the pair as a query (…/maps?q=40.7580,-73.9855), OpenStreetMap's as marker parameters (mlat/mlon plus a #map= zoom fragment), Bing's as a centre parameter. Different syntax, identical point — the generator knows each dialect so you never hand-type one.
A link at zoom 17 opens on the building; at zoom 12, on the district. Setting the zoom when you generate the link is choosing how much context your recipient lands in.

faq: Google Maps, OpenStreetMap and Bing Maps — the three link formats the tool generates cover the overwhelming majority of phones and desktops your recipients will use.
Can I set the zoom in the link?
Yes — the zoom you choose is written into the formats that support it, so the recipient lands at your intended context level rather than the provider's default.
Do recipients need an account or app?
No. The links open in a browser; the matching app intercepts them on phones that have it, which is a convenience, not a requirement.
How precise is the shared point?
Exactly the pair you entered — links share coordinates losslessly. The pair's own accuracy is your source's business; round it deliberately with the precision tools if the point is sensitive.
Can I share my live location this way?
This generator shares a fixed point you type in. Live, moving location sharing is your messaging app's feature — use that when the point moves.
The link opens the wrong side of the world.
Check the signs: western longitudes and southern latitudes are negative. A missing minus mirrors the point across the meridian — the classic link bug, visible in the pair before you send.
Providers' own share buttons shorten; a generated full link pastes into any shortener. The full form has the virtue of showing its destination — recipients can see the coordinates before tapping.
